description.narrative: (Yemen): USAID's Gateway to Education Program supports Yemen's Transition Education Plan-a national policy instrument developed as a multi-stakeholder plan to maintain progress towards literacy and longer-term educational goals in Yemen. Through Gateway, USAID aims to increase access to quality education in Yemen where nearly two million children are out of school and most lack basic services such as clean water and nutrition due to a protracted seven-year conflict...With FY 2022 education-earmarked funds, it is anticipated that the activity will 1) Develop, produce and distribute teaching and learning materials for grade 1-3 literacy and mathematics, including reviewing, updating, and adapting previously developed materials; 2) Integrate current efforts to educate out-of-school children (OOSC) through non-formal education and to prevent dropout through remedial educational programs with efforts to strengthen the formal school system (i.e. supporting entry and retention in the formal system for OOSC); 3) Work with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to provide teacher development and training to strengthen education service delivery; 4) Facilitate the involvement of families and communities in supporting their children's education; 5) Rehabilitate and equip learning spaces to support improved education provision; and 6) Increase access for vulnerable groups including support for children with disabilities, girls, and conflict affected youth and their families..Activities will result in a strengthened, more resilient education system that provides a range of services to meet the complex learning needs of the children of Yemen, many of whom have experienced disruptions to their education during the ongoing conflict. The activities directly contribute to USAID's 2018 Global Education Policy and the priorities of the MOE as laid out in its Transition Education Plan..
